text: Dawn irrigation started when the header valve opened and water climbed the drip pipe.
A cracked pump housing sprayed the tomato benches before anyone reached the aisle.
She throttled the zone valve so the far pipe would not starve the seedlings.
Algae filmed the water tank that fed the recirculating pump.
Misters fogged the cuttings whenever the solenoid valve clicked on.
Gravel in the return pipe slowed the pump and the benches dried unevenly.
The night attendant bled air from a gurgling lateral after replacing a valve.
Fertilizer stock sat beside the injector where the main water pipe entered.
Lock keepers cracked the paddle valve and water lifted the barge in the chamber.
A bargee cleared weed from the pump intake before the bywash pipe overflowed.
The ground paddle stuck, so the valve chest had to be drained of water by hand.
Towpath walkers watched water rise through an old pipe under the brick bridge.
Silt choked the culvert and the auxiliary pump ran until dusk.
Grease on the valve spindle made the gate creep while water still poured.
Winter ice split a clay pipe that fed the side pond above the lock.
The lengthsman recorded which pump had failed along the summit pound.
The printer rolled tusche ink across the limestone and waited for it to dry.
Gum arabic protected the undrawn surface before the etching bath.
A sponged stone printed a gray scum where the ink had crept.
Registration pins kept the second color from drifting on the tympan.
The scraper bar was tightened until the proof pulled clean.
Newsprint packing under the stone changed the bite of the crayon.
She grained the stone with carborundum until the old image disappeared.
Shop towels stained with ink hung beside the leather nap roller.
The marionette control bar twisted and the left string went slack.
Backstage, a puppeteer whispered cues through the booth curtain.
A tangled shoulder string made the wooden soldier bow too early.
Footlights warmed the proscenium while the bridge was still dark.
The booth frame wobbled when both operators leaned on the playboard.
Horsehair loops replaced a frayed wrist string before the matinee.
Children answered the swazzle voice from the front benches.
Paint flaked from the puppet cheek where the gauze had worn through.
The pendulum clock lost minutes after the suspension spring slipped.
A watchmaker broached the bushing where the clock arbor had worn oval.
Chime hammers stuck against the rack and the quarter struck late.
He pegged the pivot holes and refit the escape wheel of the clock.
Weights descended the clock case until the gut line wanted shortening.
Oil on the pallet stones crawled and the clock beat grew uneven.
A hairspring clung to the regulator pins and the rate wandered.
The tower trainee counted teeth on the great wheel and checked each pivot.
Indigo vats were skimmed at dawn and the flower returned blue.
Wool skeins took madder after a long mordant in alum.
The dyer lifted the skeins on sticks so the rinse would not felt the yarn.
A weak copperas bath turned the indigo cloth a dull olive.
Steam coils under the beck kept the woad dye from cooling.
Excess pigment settled and left a tide mark on the linen yarn.
She soured the silk skeins in a bran liquor before the next dip.
Dried hanks of indigo yarn were weighed against the lot card.
